title: Finance Settings
subtitle: A walkthrough for Finance Teams · Org Settings → Finance

intro.title: Org Settings → Finance
lines: A walkthrough built for finance teams —
GL codes, transaction rules, and who should have access.
intro.narration: Welcome — this walkthrough is built for finance teams setting up the Finance section of the Rec admin. We'll build out your GL codes, configure transaction rules, and cover our recommended permissions, so you know exactly who should have access to what.

steps.title: GL Library · Chart of Accounts
lines: Build your master list of GL accounts here — name plus GL code.
Once it's set up, these codes populate dropdown menus everywhere:
programs, facilities, memberships, tickets, and store items and fees.
steps.narration: Start in the GL Library with your Chart of Accounts — your master list of general ledger accounts, each with a name and a GL code. Once you've built this out, those codes show up in dropdown menus everywhere your programming staff works: on programs, facilities, memberships, tickets, and store items and fees.

steps.title: Transaction Rules · Processing Fee
lines: The processing fee on online payments — the rate is edited by
customer support, but you choose the GL code it posts to.
steps.narration: Next, transaction fees. On the Processing Fee page, the fee percentage itself is set by customer support, but your finance team chooses the GL code it posts to.

steps.title: Transaction Rules · Tax
lines: Choose the GL code for tax — inherit it from each tax item,
or apply one global GL code across all taxable transactions.
steps.narration: The Tax page controls the GL code used for tax. Inherit the code from each individual tax item, or apply one global GL code across every taxable transaction.

steps.title: Transaction Rules · Ticket Service Fee
lines: Toggle whether the 2% ticket service fee (min $0.50) is passed to
customers or absorbed by the org — and set its GL code.
steps.narration: Ticket Service Fee lets you decide whether that two percent fee, with a fifty cent minimum, is passed on to customers at checkout or absorbed by your organization, and you set the GL code it posts to.

steps.title: Transaction Rules · Desk Location
lines: Require staff to select a desk location before taking a payment.
We recommend finance teams require this, for cleaner cash-drawer reconciliation.
steps.narration: Desk Location requires staff to select a location before processing any payment. We recommend finance teams require this — it makes reconciling cash drawers by location much easier.

steps.title: Transaction Rules · Price Override
lines: Prompt staff for a reason and note whenever they override a price.
We also recommend finance teams require this, for a clean audit trail.
steps.narration: And Price Override prompts staff for a reason and a note whenever they override a price. We recommend requiring this too, so every price change leaves a clear audit trail.

steps.title: Org Settings
lines: Now let's look at who can actually access these finance controls.
steps.narration: Now let's look at who can actually access these finance controls — that's managed under Roles and Permissions.

steps.title: Org Settings · Roles and Permissions
lines: Build custom roles with exactly the access each team needs.
This org already has a Finance Team role set up — let's open it.
steps.narration: Roles and Permissions is where you build custom roles with exactly the access each team needs. This org already has a Finance Team role configured — let's open it.

steps.title: Roles and Permissions · Finance Team
lines: Our recommended finance access: edit items, finance settings, and GL codes;
process payments, issue refunds, override prices, and manage account
credits and promo codes.
steps.narration: This is our recommended finance permission set. Under Settings: the ability to create and edit items, finance settings, and GL codes. And under Payment: process payments, issue refunds, override prices at checkout, manually enter a credit card, and manage account credits and promo codes.
